request.spec:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A person may have an approver: a user name on the row (an entry and a button; APPROVER_SET
name=<name> user=<user>). That user may approve or reject the person's PENDING claims as a steward
may (the opener and the last editor still may not approve their own).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added person approvers, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What changed:**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V106__person_approver.sql`, adds a nullable `approver` column to the `person` table. Like the flag, changing it doesn't bump the person's version.
- **Server:**
  - `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/people/{id}/approver` sets the approver. A blank name clears it.
  - Each change writes `APPROVER_SET sheet=… by=… name=<person> user=<user>` to the audit file.
  - The person view now includes `approver`.
- **Who may approve or reject:** in `ClaimService`, a PENDING claim can now be approved or rejected by a steward *or* by the user named as that person's approver. The existing rule that the opener or last editor can't approve their own claim still applies to approvers too.
- **Front end:** each person row has a new Approver column with `person-approver` (the current approver), `person-approver-input` and `person-approver-save`. A failure shows in the row's existing `person-error`. I also reworded the refusal message for approve/reject in the claims screen to mention the approver.

**Choices the request left open:**
- **Anyone except a viewer can set an approver.** The test has a clerk (uma) set it, so I didn't limit it to stewards. Viewers and archived sheets are still blocked by the app's existing guards.
- **Blank clears the approver.** It's accepted rather than refused, and the audit line then ends with an empty `user=`.
- **Not carried into other features:** the approver isn't copied when a sheet is cloned and isn't part of the as-of history. The flag works the same way.
